title: Remove K Digits
summary: Given a string representing a non-negative integer and an integer k, remove exactly k digits to form the smallest possible integer.
statement: Given a string representing a non-negative integer and an integer k, remove exactly k digits to form the smallest possible integer.
constraints: 1 <= k <= num.length <= 100,000; num contains decimal digits only.
The input has no leading zeros unless it is "0". Remove exactly k digits without reordering survivors.
Return a decimal string with no leading zeros; an empty or all-zero result is "0".
hints: A smaller earlier digit improves the result more than any later digit.
Maintain a nondecreasing stack, removing larger preceding digits while deletions remain.
For each digit, pop larger stack tops while k>0, then append. Remove any leftover k digits from the end and strip leading zeros.
Each digit is pushed and popped at most once. Preserve equal earlier digits, remove exactly k total, and avoid converting the huge number to an integer.
editorial: When a smaller digit arrives, removing a larger preceding digit improves the earliest possible position. A monotone stack applies this exchange greedily. If deletions remain, the remaining sequence is nondecreasing, so delete from its end. Normalize leading zeros only after the required deletions. All work stays on strings, supporting 100,000-digit inputs.

tests.explanation: Remove 4, 3, and one 2 while preserving the remaining order, yielding 1219.
Removing the leading 1 leaves 0200, which is normalized to the string "200".
